hook: An X-point target divertor cut peak outer heat flux by 40 to 60% in high-power tokamak tests.
summary: A tokamak exhaust design called the X-point target was compared with a conventional single-null divertor at 2.5 MW on the TCV tokamak. It lowered peak outer target heat flux and allowed detachment with nitrogen seeding where the conventional design could not. Reversing the magnetic field showed that E x B drifts cause uneven detachment across strike points. The tests were in L-mode on one machine, which is smaller than a reactor.
title: High-power X-Point Target divertor experiments on the TCV tokamak
